bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body: - Ongoing program to reduce interest cost/finance costs alongside continued reinvestment into capacity expansion (new Shikrapur facility) to support future growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Over five decades (57+ years) of experience in precision aluminium castings, and early pioneer status in LPDC and Gravity Die Casting in India
- Integrated end-to-end capability spanning prototype and tool design, simulation, tool manufacturing, fixture design, casting, VA/VE, machining, sub-assembly, painting and surface treatment, reducing handoffs and catching issues earlier than a single-stage supplier
- Deliberately broad customer base: 91 customers across 18 countries with over 801 live parts, so that no single customer, geography or platform represents a disproportionate share
- Diversified across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, Tier-1 suppliers and non-automotive applications
- Group ecosystem combining European engineering precision (Illichmann Castalloy), Japanese manufacturing excellence (Enkei Corporation association) and Indian cost-efficient innovation, plus tooling partner Atlas Castalloy
- Executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 Crore providing medium-term revenue visibility through FY 2030-31
- Growing participation in EV, hybrid and e-Axle programmes, including a recently secured global EV platform business
- More than 50% of power requirement met through renewable energy, reducing energy cost exposure
- Long-term credit rating reaffirmed by CRISIL at CRISIL A/Positive and short-term facilities at CRISIL A1
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitical and trade risk — Global geopolitical developments, including trade tariff uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures, may affect exports, raw material availability and customer demand, influencing operations in both domestic and international markets. Mitigated through presence across 18 countries reducing dependence on any single market, continuous monitoring of geopolitical developments and business continuity plans.
- Demand slowdown risk — Economic slowdown, inflationary pressures and changing market conditions may affect demand across automotive and industrial sectors, impacting production volumes and revenue. Mitigated by diversifying the customer base, product portfolio and end-use industries, with an executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 Crore providing medium-term revenue visibility.
- Raw material price volatility and availability — Availability of raw materials and volatility in aluminium and alloy prices may affect production costs and profitability, while supply disruptions may impact manufacturing schedules. Mitigated by standardising alloy variants to optimise material usage and by raw material pass-through clauses in customer contracts, though the SWOT notes margins may still be affected despite contractual pass-through mechanisms.
- Competition risk — Increasing competition from domestic and global foundries and manufacturers may exert pressure on pricing, market share and customer acquisition. Differentiation relies on integrated engineering capabilities, advanced manufacturing technologies and over five decades of industry experience.
- Supply chain risk (newly added this year) — Global logistics disruptions, component shortages and supplier-related challenges may affect production schedules and programme execution. Mitigated by diversifying the supplier base, strengthening customer coordination, improving production planning and enhancing operational flexibility.
- Automotive sector concentration — A significant portion of revenue is derived from the automotive sector - approximately 95% of FY 2025-26 revenue with only 5% from non-automotive applications - making the business sensitive to automotive industry cycles.
- Capital intensity and capacity expansion execution — Continuous investment in automation, advanced machining and capacity expansion may impact near-term profitability, while delays in capacity expansion could limit the Company's ability to capitalise on increasing customer enquiries and new business opportunities.
- Export market and currency exposure — International operations remain susceptible to geopolitical developments, freight disruptions and currency fluctuations; rising labour costs and other operating expenses may also affect margins until productivity improvements are fully realised.
- Product quality, safety and reliability — Identified as a material issue in the BRSR: quality issues may lead to product rejections, warranty claims, recalls and increased manufacturing costs; failure to meet customer specifications or industry quality standards could affect long-term relationships with OEMs and Tier-1 customers and limit future business.
- Energy cost and availability — Aluminium casting involves energy-intensive melting, heat treatment and machining, making energy a significant operating cost; fluctuations in electricity and fuel prices directly impact manufacturing costs, and any disruption in energy availability could affect production continuity and long-term competitiveness.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Domestic: 80% of revenue; PV: strong SUV/hybrid demand; CV: +19.5% YoY volume growth; 2W: material contribution increase in Q4; Export: softness due to geopolitical headwinds; New: first non-auto win in data center turbo core compressor
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Pioneer in India for Low Pressure Die Casting (LPDC) and Gravity Die Casting (GDC); operates one of the largest aluminum foundries in India.
- Leader in the development of Pro-Cast and Magma space in India, with a diversified, marquee customer base and no reliance on a single anchor customer.
- 56-year track record, further enriched by the 89-year legacy of European subsidiary Illichmann Castalloy; group blends European engineering, Japanese quality (via Enkei) and Indian frugal engineering across 235+ cumulative years of experience.
- 4 modern manufacturing plants (3 in India - Pune x2, Binola; 1 international - Slovakia) plus an international marketing office in Austria, enabling a 'close-to-demand' global footprint for shorter time-to-market and cost optimisation.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body: - [Leadership] CEO Sumit Bhatnagar highlighted the new Shikrapur-area facility as a strategic step to support future growth, alongside continued focus on customer partnerships, manufacturing capabilities and building a scalable organisation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Alicon designs, casts, machines and assembles precision aluminium components for automotive OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers across two-, three- and four-wheelers, and for non-automotive customers in infrastructure, defence, aerospace, energy, agriculture, medical and carbon-neutral technologies. It was among India's early pioneers in Low Pressure Die Casting (LPDC) and Gravity Die Casting (GDC), and its capabilities span the full product lifecycle from prototype and tool design and simulation through casting, VA/VE, machining, sub-assembly, painting and surface treatment. During FY 2025-26 it served 91 customers through a portfolio of over 801 live production parts.

business.body:

- **Electric and hybrid mobility:** Battery Tray, Battery enclosures, Motor Housing, Motor Stator, Inverter Casing, Controller Housing, E-axle, eAxle housings, Cooling/Junction Box
- **Non-automotive:** Precision-cast component for data-centre infrastructure, Cac Tank, Enclosure Body, Roof sensor housing for autonomous car

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- FY 2026-27 strategic theme is 'Reset, Refocus and Rebuild', with priorities of establishing at least one new manufacturing facility, expanding automation and machining capabilities, and strengthening technology, processes and human capital.
- Strengthen the core ICE and domestic business: ramp cylinder head volumes for a leading Japanese OEM's 1.5-litre engine platform, and retain the 100% share of cylinder head business for another Japanese OEM's hybrid vehicle platform.
- Remain deliberately technology-agnostic across internal combustion, hybrid and electric architectures rather than concentrating bets on any single technology.
- Deepen existing customer relationships while expanding into new geographies and industry segments, pursuing opportunities across Europe and the U.S.
- Increase the manufacturing footprint, first within Maharashtra and potentially thereafter in other strategic locations outside the state, to be closer to customers and create capacity ahead of programme requirements.
- Invest in automation, advanced manufacturing technologies and machining capabilities to move further up the value chain, creating smarter and more productive capacity through greater robotisation, digitisation and process automation.
- Diversify beyond automotive: entry into data-centre infrastructure components and advancement of the Defence, Aerospace and Railways (DAR) vertical from initial engagements to active pilot programmes.
- Advance electrification participation, having secured a new e-Axle housing programme from a premium German OEM for an electric vehicle platform.
- Strengthen R&D and engineering capabilities to participate earlier in customers' product-development journeys and develop increasingly complex, higher-value components.
- Reduce operational expenditure through Kaizen methodologies, lean and agile manufacturing, overhead and fixed cost optimisation, interest cost optimisation and energy mix diversification.
- Improve order quality and execution certainty: a comprehensive fourth-quarter review of the order pipeline produced a validated, executable order book.
- Build a future-ready organisation, having strengthened the leadership team across sales and marketing, product and process technology, programme management, manufacturing, supply chain, tool manufacturing, operational excellence and human resources.
- Embed sustainability, with more than 50% of electricity across Indian and European facilities sourced from renewable energy and an EcoVadis 'Committed' recognition placing the Company among the top 35% of companies globally assessed.
- Long-term ambition over three to five years is to become a technology-led, globally-relevant manufacturing partner to automotive and select non-automotive customers, not merely a larger aluminium casting company.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Alicon operates four modern manufacturing facilities - three in India (Chinchwad and Shikrapur in Pune, Maharashtra, and Binola in Haryana) and one in Slovakia - supported by advanced technology centres, globally competitive tool rooms, product validation laboratories, machine shops and assembly facilities, plus an international marketing office in Austria. During FY 2025-26 the Company continued to invest in maintenance, automation, capacity enhancement and new product programmes, with capital expenditure focused on advanced manufacturing technologies, automation and capacity creation for complex aluminium casting applications requiring higher machining content. Manufacturing facilities operated at an average capacity utilisation of around 78% during the year. Looking forward, the FY 2026-27 strategic theme 'Reset, Refocus and Rebuild' includes establishing at least one new manufacturing facility and expanding automation and machining capabilities. The Managing Director stated that as customer programmes and the order pipeline grow, Alicon is already increasing its manufacturing footprint, first within Maharashtra and potentially thereafter in other strategic locations outside the state, in order to be closer to customers and create capacity ahead of programme requirements; this expansion will be pursued in a disciplined manner aligned with customer requirements. The Company also flagged Capacity Expansion as an opportunity, noting that planned investments in a new manufacturing facility will support future business growth and execution of the existing order book, while listing Capacity Constraints as a threat since delays in capacity expansion could limit its ability to capitalise on increasing customer enquiries. Ongoing programme-level expansion includes commencement of supplies for the Daimler programme (around 60% of planned parts PPAP-approved, the remainder expected to be commercialised over the next two quarters), continued advancement of Jaguar Land Rover programmes, a new e-Axle housing programme from a premium German OEM, and the first order for a precision-cast component for data-centre infrastructure. On the energy side, an express feeder was commissioned during the reporting year to ensure continuous grid electricity supply, significantly reducing reliance on diesel generator sets; the Company is progressively replacing LPG and LSHS with Piped Natural Gas by modifying existing furnaces, and continues to add rooftop solar and green power procurement. A 26%-held associate SPV, Radiance MH Sunrise Three Private Limited, supplies solar power of up to 12 MW to the Shikrapur and Chinchwad plants in Maharashtra.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The domestic market is expected to remain the primary growth driver, while the Company continues to pursue opportunities in Europe and the U.S.
- Increasing enquiries across new platforms, geographies and product segments, together with the executable order book, provide strong medium-term growth visibility.
- For FY 2026-27 the Company expects revenue growth of around 8-10%, excluding the impact of aluminium price movements, supported by a healthy order pipeline and sustained customer demand.
- Focus on productivity, operational efficiency and margin improvement through ongoing investments in automation and capacity expansion, while remaining watchful of geopolitical developments, raw material price volatility and inflationary pressures.
- Structural trends of vehicle electrification, hybrid mobility, lightweight engineering, localisation and global supply chain diversification are creating opportunities for companies with advanced aluminium casting capabilities.
- The India+1/China+1 sourcing strategy is creating opportunities to expand business with global OEMs.
- Automotive contributed 95% of FY 2025-26 revenue and the domestic market approximately 87% of business; consumer preference shifting towards SUVs supported cylinder head volume ramp-up for a leading Japanese OEM.
- Improving domestic demand and GST rationalisation from September onwards supported core business momentum.
- Rising adoption of electric, hybrid, fuel-cell and hydrogen-powered vehicles is increasing demand for lightweight aluminium castings.
- Growing opportunities in industrial, energy and data-centre cooling applications can diversify the revenue base.
- Non-automotive contribution of 5% of FY 2025-26 revenue is expected to increase over the coming years as newer programmes mature and the DAR business scales.
- Margin moderation in FY 2025-26 was attributed to higher aluminium prices, changes in product mix, increased logistics and packaging costs and certain one-time expenses.
- Customers increasingly engage with Alicon as long-term engineering and manufacturing partners rather than component suppliers, creating opportunities to expand programme and platform scope.
- A validated, executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 Crore for the period from FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31, providing long-term revenue visibility.
- During the fourth quarter the Company undertook a comprehensive review of its order pipeline to improve execution certainty and strengthen order quality, resulting in an executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 crore with visibility through FY 2031.
- During the fourth quarter the Company secured two new domestic business wins, comprising one component each for the internal combustion engine (ICE) and non-automotive segments.
- The Company continued to pursue additional opportunities across Europe and the U.S. to further strengthen its order pipeline.
- Secured a new e-Axle housing programme from a premium German OEM for an electric vehicle platform.
- Secured the first order for a precision-cast component used in data-centre infrastructure, marking entry into an entirely new application segment.
- Supplies commenced for the Daimler programme during the year, with around 60% of planned parts having received PPAP approval; programmes for Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) and other global customers continued to advance.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Alicon delivered record Q4 revenue driven by domestic automotive recovery and new non-auto wins, but margins were pressured by aluminum price lags and one-off labor cost hikes; the company is now resetting strategy with capacity expansion, automation, and renewed focus on India to unlock long-term growth from a ₹7,600 crore order book.

currentContext.expansion: Alicon operates four modern manufacturing facilities - three in India (Chinchwad and Shikrapur in Pune, Maharashtra, and Binola in Haryana) and one in Slovakia - supported by advanced technology centres, globally competitive tool rooms, product validation laboratories, machine shops and assembly facilities, plus an international marketing office in Austria. During FY 2025-26 the Company continued to invest in maintenance, automation, capacity enhancement and new product programmes, with capital expenditure focused on advanced manufacturing technologies, automation and capacity creation for complex aluminium casting applications requiring higher machining content. Manufacturing facilities operated at an average capacity utilisation of around 78% during the year. Looking forward, the FY 2026-27 strategic theme 'Reset, Refocus and Rebuild' includes establishing at least one new manufacturing facility and expanding automation and machining capabilities. The Managing Director stated that as customer programmes and the order pipeline grow, Alicon is already increasing its manufacturing footprint, first within Maharashtra and potentially thereafter in other strategic locations outside the state, in order to be closer to customers and create capacity ahead of programme requirements; this expansion will be pursued in a disciplined manner aligned with customer requirements. The Company also flagged Capacity Expansion as an opportunity, noting that planned investments in a new manufacturing facility will support future business growth and execution of the existing order book, while listing Capacity Constraints as a threat since delays in capacity expansion could limit its ability to capitalise on increasing customer enquiries. Ongoing programme-level expansion includes commencement of supplies for the Daimler programme (around 60% of planned parts PPAP-approved, the remainder expected to be commercialised over the next two quarters), continued advancement of Jaguar Land Rover programmes, a new e-Axle housing programme from a premium German OEM, and the first order for a precision-cast component for data-centre infrastructure. On the energy side, an express feeder was commissioned during the reporting year to ensure continuous grid electricity supply, significantly reducing reliance on diesel generator sets; the Company is progressively replacing LPG and LSHS with Piped Natural Gas by modifying existing furnaces, and continues to add rooftop solar and green power procurement. A 26%-held associate SPV, Radiance MH Sunrise Three Private Limited, supplies solar power of up to 12 MW to the Shikrapur and Chinchwad plants in Maharashtra.

risks.note: Global geopolitical developments, including trade tariff uncertainties, supply chain disruptions and inflationary pressures, may affect exports, raw material availability and customer demand, influencing operations in both domestic and international markets. Mitigated through presence across 18 countries reducing dependence on any single market, continuous monitoring of geopolitical developments and business continuity plans.

Economic slowdown, inflationary pressures and changing market conditions may affect demand across automotive and industrial sectors, impacting production volumes and revenue. Mitigated by diversifying the customer base, product portfolio and end-use industries, with an executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 Crore providing medium-term revenue visibility.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and availability
risks.note: Availability of raw materials and volatility in aluminium and alloy prices may affect production costs and profitability, while supply disruptions may impact manufacturing schedules. Mitigated by standardising alloy variants to optimise material usage and by raw material pass-through clauses in customer contracts, though the SWOT notes margins may still be affected despite contractual pass-through mechanisms.

Increasing competition from domestic and global foundries and manufacturers may exert pressure on pricing, market share and customer acquisition. Differentiation relies on integrated engineering capabilities, advanced manufacturing technologies and over five decades of industry experience.

risks.risk: Supply chain risk (newly added this year)
risks.note: Global logistics disruptions, component shortages and supplier-related challenges may affect production schedules and programme execution. Mitigated by diversifying the supplier base, strengthening customer coordination, improving production planning and enhancing operational flexibility.

A significant portion of revenue is derived from the automotive sector - approximately 95% of FY 2025-26 revenue with only 5% from non-automotive applications - making the business sensitive to automotive industry cycles.

risks.risk: Capital intensity and capacity expansion execution
risks.note: Continuous investment in automation, advanced machining and capacity expansion may impact near-term profitability, while delays in capacity expansion could limit the Company's ability to capitalise on increasing customer enquiries and new business opportunities.

International operations remain susceptible to geopolitical developments, freight disruptions and currency fluctuations; rising labour costs and other operating expenses may also affect margins until productivity improvements are fully realised.

Identified as a material issue in the BRSR: quality issues may lead to product rejections, warranty claims, recalls and increased manufacturing costs; failure to meet customer specifications or industry quality standards could affect long-term relationships with OEMs and Tier-1 customers and limit future business.

Aluminium casting involves energy-intensive melting, heat treatment and machining, making energy a significant operating cost; fluctuations in electricity and fuel prices directly impact manufacturing costs, and any disruption in energy availability could affect production continuity and long-term competitiveness.

one-line thesis: Alicon delivered record Q4 revenue driven by domestic automotive recovery and new non-auto wins, but margins were pressured by aluminum price lags and one-off labor cost hikes; the company is now resetting strategy with capacity expansion, automation, and renewed focus on India to unlock long-term growth from a ₹7,600 crore order book.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Alicon Castalloy is a Pune-headquartered integrated manufacturer of precision aluminium castings and one of India's largest players in the industry, serving customers across 18 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Alicon designs, casts, machines and assembles precision aluminium components for automotive OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers across two-, three- and four-wheelers, and for non-automotive customers in infrastructure, defence, aerospace, energy, agriculture, medical and carbon-neutral technologies. It was among India's early pioneers in Low Pressure Die Casting (LPDC) and Gravity Die Casting (GDC), and its capabilities span the full product lifecycle from prototype and tool design and simulation through casting, VA/VE, machining, sub-assembly, painting and surface treatment. During FY 2025-26 it served 91 customers through a portfolio of over 801 live production parts.

- Secured a new e-Axle housing programme from a premium German OEM for an electric vehicle platform.
- Secured the first order for a precision-cast component used in data-centre infrastructure, marking entry into an entirely new application segment.
- Supplies commenced for the Daimler programme during the year, with around 60% of planned parts having received PPAP approval; programmes for Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) and other global customers continued to advance.

- Deliberately broad customer base: 91 customers across 18 countries with over 801 live parts, so that no single customer, geography or platform represents a disproportionate share
- Diversified across two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, Tier-1 suppliers and non-automotive applications
- Group ecosystem combining European engineering precision (Illichmann Castalloy), Japanese manufacturing excellence (Enkei Corporation association) and Indian cost-efficient innovation, plus tooling partner Atlas Castalloy
- Executable order book of approximately Rs 7,600 Crore providing medium-term revenue visibility through FY 2030-31
- Growing participation in EV, hybrid and e-Axle programmes, including a recently secured global EV platform business
- More than 50% of power requirement met through renewable energy, reducing energy cost exposure
- Long-term credit rating reaffirmed by CRISIL at CRISIL A/Positive and short-term facilities at CRISIL A1

one-line thesis: Alicon delivered record Q4 revenue driven by domestic automotive recovery and new non-auto wins, but margins were pressured by aluminum price lags and one-off labor cost hikes; the company is now resetting strategy with capacity expansion, automation, and renewed focus on India to unlock long-term growth from a ₹7,600 crore order book.
financial scorecard: revenue: +16% YoY (₹495cr Q4); EBITDA/margin: -3% YoY (₹46cr), 45% gross margin (down 248bps YoY); PAT (rptd): -11% YoY (₹8cr); PAT (normalized): +141% QoQ (excl. ₹26cr one-off expenses); order book: ₹7,600cr (6-year visibility); net debt: not disclosed, but capex ₹135cr FY26 with strong working capital discipline
guidance: revenue growth: 8-10% FY27 (excl. aluminum volatility); margin: expecting 1.5%+ EBITDA margin expansion; order inflow: new wins in EV axle (Germany), data center turbo core, premium 2W; capex/commissioning: ₹130-150cr FY27 for new plant, automation, machining, cybersecurity
order book & pipeline: ₹7,600 crore executable order book (FY26-FY31), excludes pre-FY26 revenue programs; includes new wins: German e-Axle housing, data center turbo core, premium Indian 2W part; rationalized 4 non-performing global/Indian programs
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic: 80% of revenue; PV: strong SUV/hybrid demand; CV: +19.5% YoY volume growth; 2W: material contribution increase in Q4; Export: softness due to geopolitical headwinds; New: first non-auto win in data center turbo core compressor
growth verticals / optionality: New manufacturing plant (1+ by FY27), entry into data center components, deeper penetration in Indian OEMs previously untapped, European EV/ICE program ramp-up, potential forward integration
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin down 248bps YoY due to aluminum price pass-through lag (₹30-35cr Q4 impact), labor cost hike of 35% at Binola plant (Haryana wage code), energy/freight inflation; EBITDA margin pressured by mix shift to domestic/2W and one-off ₹26cr FY26 expenses
capex / expansion: FY26: ₹135cr; FY27 guidance: ₹130-150cr; allocation: new plant (1+), die casting & machining capacity, automation (core focus), cybersecurity, R&D/digital manufacturing
capital allocation: Dividend recommended: ₹2/share FY26; capex prioritized over buybacks; no M&A mentioned; focus on organic growth and operational efficiency
risks & watch-items: Aluminum price volatility (pass-through lag), labor cost escalation across states, geopolitical supply chain disruptions, delayed global program ramp-ups (e.g., JLR), margin compression from input inflation
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; CEO Sumit Bhatnagar emphasized 'Refocus, Reset, Rebuild' with disciplined execution; acknowledged past global missteps but confident in domestic rebound and new capacity; tone pragmatic, not overly bullish

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

hero.oneLiner: Alicon Castalloy is a Pune-headquartered integrated manufacturer of precision aluminium castings and one of India's largest players in the industry, serving customers across 18 countries.
